events.credibility_reason: No official completion report; double-checking of the 2020-2022 run unstated, and the earlier PRPNet run was abandoned as unreliable. The 2^64 figure rests on OEIS and Wikipedia.
Single-author independent preprint; v2 downgraded a theorem to a conjecture; minimality deferred to an unwritten companion paper. Irrelevant to the integer question in any case.

why: The statement is a single existence question about integer primes satisfying both congruences. The base-2 searches (1997, 2005, 2011, PrimeGrid 2022) exclude joint primes only below a finite height, so they are finite instance checks (F5), not bounds on a quantity the statement asks for, and all predate the snapshot anyway. Dobson's sharpened criteria settle nothing (none). Every post-snapshot event concerns a function-field or number-field analogue, so each is a variant. For Giraudin, the basis quote ('in sustained collaboration with an AI assistant') does not say the model produced the counterexample; the fuller description (proposed problems, domain knowledge, formalization, drafting) is thin, so I scored none — and the event is a variant of a different conjecture regardless.
doubts: Giraudin's AI role is a close call (assisted vs none) but cannot affect this problem since the event is a variant. The base-3 bound of 9.7e14 attributed to Dorais-Klyve was not confirmed in the record.
